meta.title: Operation of Melting Point Apparatus in Pharmaceutical Chemistry Laboratory

sections.purpose: To determine the melting point of synthesized pharmaceutical compounds and pure drug substances as a key identity, purity, and characterization parameter as per IP/BP/USP pharmacopeial standards.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmaceutical Chemistry laboratory for melting point determination of synthesized drug intermediates, final products, and reference standard verification.
procedure: Switch on the melting point apparatus and set the starting temperature approximately 10°C below the expected melting point of the compound.
Dry the compound thoroughly — moisture presence lowers the observed melting point significantly.
Grind a small quantity of the compound to fine powder using a mortar and pestle.
Fill a capillary tube (1 mm internal diameter, sealed at one end) by pressing the open end into the powder heap repeatedly.
Compact the powder by dropping the capillary tube (closed end down) repeatedly through a long glass tube onto the bench — compact to 2–3 mm column height.
Place the capillary tube in the heating block or silicon oil bath of the apparatus.
Set the heating rate to 1–2°C/minute as the expected melting point is approached — slow heating rates give more accurate results.
Observe the capillary tube through the magnifying eyepiece.
Note the temperature when the compound first begins to soften or shows the first drop of liquid at the edges (onset of melting, T₁).
Note the temperature when the compound becomes completely liquid (complete melting, T₂).
The melting range is reported as T₁–T₂ (e.g., 154–156°C).
A narrow melting range (≤ 2°C) indicates high purity; a wide range suggests impurities or mixed crystal forms.
Compare the observed melting point with the reference value from the pharmacopoeia or literature.
Allow the apparatus to cool before the next determination.
Record: compound name, batch, expected MP, observed MP range, and purity inference in the laboratory notebook.
precautions: For capillary tube method, use only calibrated, clean capillary tubes — reusing tubes introduces contamination.
Ensure the compound is finely powdered and packed tightly — loosely packed powder gives a wide, inaccurate melting range.
Use a slow heating rate (1–2°C/min) near the expected melting point — fast heating gives results 2–5°C higher than the true value.
Do not touch the capillary tube with bare hands while loading — skin oils contaminate the compound.
Do not overfill the capillary tube — the compound column should be 2–3 mm; taller columns cause slow heat transfer.
Allow the apparatus to cool completely between runs if re-running at a lower temperature.
Calibrate the apparatus regularly using reference standards (e.g., phenacetin MP 134–135°C; acetanilide 114–116°C).
